topic: Range-Based For Loop in Modern C++
explanation: The range-based for loop in C++ (introduced in C++11) provides a concise and readable syntax for iterating over all elements in a container or range. It simplifies traversal by abstracting iterator management, reducing boilerplate code, and minimizing errors associated with manual iterator handling. This feature enhances code clarity and safety, especially when working with standard library containers and modern C++ idioms.
code_example: // Using range-based for loop to print elements of coll1
// Using range-based for loop to modify elements of coll2
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the range-based for loop by iterating over a vector and a list. The first loop prints all elements of 'coll1' directly, showcasing simple traversal. The second loop modifies each element of 'coll2' by doubling its value, illustrating how the loop can be used for in-place modification with auto&. The syntax improves code readability and safety compared to traditional iterator-based loops, exemplifying modern C++ idioms for container traversal.
